note.p: Andrew Caldwell was a barrister and connoisseur of architecture, eldest child of Charles Caldwell. He attended Glasgow University between 1751 and 1754 but chose not to graduate. He studied law with his father in Dublin before moving to London, but in 1760 he was called to the Irish bar. He spent a lot of time on appreciating the arts, in particular architecture. He was a particular fan of William Chambers. He was a friend to Charlotte Smith, who he appeared with in Godwin’s first entry mentioning him, and was mentioned in her Collected Letters. There's an issue as to whether it is Andrew Caldwell or John Caldwell that Godwin meets in the company of Curran on his Irish trip. The later resides at Castle Caldwell which is a considerable distance from Rathfarnham, making Andrew more probable. (see John Caldwell (1756=1830), eldest son of Sir James Caldwell (1720-1784, army officer who developed strong interests in native American peoples).
